title: Open images of restricted smooth atlases
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $\mathcal X$ be an algebraic stack over $S$: a stack in groupoids for etale coverings, with diagonal representable by algebraic spaces and a representable smooth surjective scheme atlas. Stacks, representability and 2-fibre products use [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids], and algebraic spaces use [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Let $p:U\to\mathcal X$ be a representable smooth surjective atlas from a scheme, and let $j:V\hookrightarrow U$ be an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. Then $p\circ j$ is representable and smooth, and factors through an algebraic open substack $\mathcal W\subseteq\mathcal X$ as a representable smooth surjection $V\to\mathcal W$. An open substack is a strictly full substack whose pullback by every scheme is an open subscheme. For every scheme $T\to\mathcal X$, the open subscheme $T\times_{\mathcal X}\mathcal W$ is the open image of the algebraic-space map $V\times_{\mathcal X}T\to T$. Smoothness of representable maps is tested after scheme base change on etale scheme charts, using [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]; surjectivity means surjectivity on points after every scheme base change. Empty $V$ is allowed.

source.place: Tag 05UP (lemma-open-image-substack), statement and proof, especially the definition of the fibre category and T_0 as the image of V times_X T to T. Smoothness of the composite is the open restriction in that proof, using morphisms.tex Tag 01VC (lemma-open-immersion-smooth). For the etale-stack convention, criteria.tex Tag 076V (lemma-stacks-etale) identifies it with the fppf algebraic-stack convention.

proof.text: Put $g=p\circ j$. The open immersion $j$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation](1), hence smooth by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. It is representable by schemes: its scheme pullbacks are the inverse-image open subschemes. The composition assertion of the same calculus node, applied to $j$ and $p$, makes $g$ representable by algebraic spaces and smooth.

For a scheme $T$ and $x:T\to\mathcal X$, let $E_x=V\times_{\mathcal X,x}T$ and $a_x:E_x\to T$. Representability of $g$ makes $E_x$ an algebraic space. Base change in [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus] makes $a_x$ smooth, hence flat and locally of finite presentation. Thus [lem-sfb-flat-lfp-space-universally-open] shows that $I_x=\operatorname{im}(|E_x|\to|T|)$ is open. Endow $I_x\subseteq T$ with its open subscheme structure [def-weil-open-immersion].

source.place: Tag 05UP (lemma-open-image-substack), smooth pullback and its open image; spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 042S (lemma-fppf-open)

proof.text: For $h:T\prime\to T$, reassociating the triples in the 2-fibre product [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids] gives $E_{x h}\simeq E_x\times_TT\prime$, compatibly with projection to $T\prime$. The point-image formula of [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus] gives $I_{x h}=h^{-1}(I_x)$ as subsets, hence as open subschemes. An isomorphism $x\simeq y$ induces an isomorphism $E_x\simeq E_y$ over $T$, so $I_x=I_y$. These equalities hold for arbitrary scheme maps, not just etale ones.

source.place: Tag 05UP, the two cartesian squares; spaces-properties.tex Tag 03H4 (lemma-points-cartesian), point-image base-change formula

proof.text: Define $\mathcal W(T)$ as the full subgroupoid of $\mathcal X(T)$ on objects $x$ with $I_x=T$, equivalently $a_x$ surjective on points. Step 3 makes this predicate invariant under isomorphism and stable under pullback, so it defines a strictly full fibred subcategory. It is an etale substack: isomorphism sheaves are those of $\mathcal X$; a descent datum descends in $\mathcal X$ to $x$, and its restrictions lie in $\mathcal W$ exactly when the inverse images of $I_x$ on the jointly surjective etale cover are the whole cover members. This forces $I_x=T$. These are precisely the stack conditions of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids].

source.place: Tag 05UP, definition of the fibre category, with the stack condition expanded from etale descent

proof.text: For a scheme test $x:T\to\mathcal X$, an object of $T\times_{\mathcal X}\mathcal W$ over $T\prime$ is $(h:T\prime\to T,w,\alpha:xh\simeq w)$. Step 3 makes its existence equivalent to $h^{-1}(I_x)=T\prime$, or $h(T\prime)\subseteq I_x$. By [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme], this is equivalent to a unique factorization through $I_x$. For fixed $h$, any two pairs $(w,\alpha)$ have exactly one arrow respecting their comparison maps, namely $\alpha\prime\alpha^{-1}$, because $\mathcal W$ is full. Taking $w=xh$ gives a preferred pair whenever the predicate holds. This identifies the fibre product with the discrete fibred groupoid of $I_x$, compatibly with pullbacks. Thus $\mathcal W\to\mathcal X$ is representable by open immersions, and its scheme pullback is exactly the asserted open image.

source.place: Tag 05UP, identification of the pullback with T_0; schemes.tex Tag 01HI (lemma-restrict-map-to-opens)

proof.text: The diagonal section of $V\times_{\mathcal X}V\to V$, given by $(v,v,\mathrm{id}_{g(v)})$, proves $I_g=V$. Thus the object $g\in\mathcal X(V)$ belongs to $\mathcal W(V)$ and supplies $q:V\to\mathcal W$ with composite $g$. For any scheme $T\to\mathcal W$ with underlying object $x$, full faithfulness identifies $V\times_{\mathcal W}T$ with $E_x$: the isomorphism of images in $\mathcal X$ is already an isomorphism in $\mathcal W$. Hence this is an algebraic space and its projection is the smooth $a_x$ of step 2. It is surjective since $x\in\mathcal W(T)$ means $I_x=T$. Therefore $q$ is representable, smooth and surjective by the scheme-test definitions.

source.place: Tag 05UP, diagonal section and final smooth-surjectivity argument

proof.text: For schemes $A,B\to\mathcal W$, full faithfulness also identifies $A\times_{\mathcal W}B$ with $A\times_{\mathcal X}B$. The latter is an algebraic space: it is a scheme pullback of the representable diagonal of $\mathcal X$. Thus the diagonal of $\mathcal W$ is representable by algebraic spaces. Together with the etale-stack condition from step 4 and the smooth surjective scheme atlas $q$ from step 6, this proves algebraicity in the statement's convention. If $V$ is empty, every $E_x$ and $I_x$ is empty; consequently $\mathcal W$ is the empty open substack and $q$ is the empty atlas. If $V=U$, the atlas hypothesis gives $I_x=T$ for every $x$, so $\mathcal W=\mathcal X$. No nonemptiness or quasi-compactness was used.

source.place: Tag 05UP, algebraicity, checked by its defining diagonal and atlas; algebraic.tex Tag 05UN (lemma-open-fibred-category-is-algebraic)

proof_origin.place: Tag 05UP (lemma-open-image-substack), proof; the etale-stack convention is handled by direct descent, and algebraicity by its diagonal and the constructed atlas.

lean.statement: theorem smooth_atlas_open_image {S : Scheme.{u}} (X : BasedCategory.{v, w} (Over S)) (hX : IsAlgebraicModuliStack X) (U V : Over S) (p : BasedFunctor (discreteModuli (yoneda.obj U)) X) (hp : IsSmoothModuliAtlas X U p) (j : V ⟶ U) (hj : IsOpenImmersion j.left) : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces ((discreteModuliMap (yoneda.map j)).comp p) ∧ ModuliSpaceTest @Smooth ((discreteModuliMap (yoneda.map j)).comp p) ∧ ∃ (W : OpenModuliSubstack X) (q : BasedFunctor (discreteModuli (yoneda.obj V)) W.category), IsAlgebraicModuliStack W.category ∧ IsSmoothModuliAtlas W.category V q ∧ Nonempty (ModuliTwoIso (q.comp (fullModuliInclusion X W.property)) ((discreteModuliMap (yoneda.map j)).comp p)) ∧ ∀ (T : Over S) (t : BasedFunctor (discreteModuli (yoneda.obj T)) X), ∃ (Z : AlgebraicSpace S) (a : Z.obj.obj ⟶ yoneda.obj T) (O : Over S) (i : O ⟶ T) (e : BasedFunctor (discreteModuli (yoneda.obj O)) (moduliTwoFiberProduct t (fullModuliInclusion X W.property))), HasSpaceBaseChange ((discreteModuliMap (yoneda.map j)).comp p) T t Z a ∧ IsOpenImmersion i.left ∧ e.toFunctor.IsEquivalence ∧ Nonempty (ModuliTwoIso (e.comp (moduliTwoFiberFst t (fullModuliInclusion X W.property))) (discreteModuliMap (yoneda.map i))) ∧ Set.range i.left = {x : T.left | ∃ (A : Over S) (b : yoneda.obj A ⟶ Z.obj.obj), AlgebraicSpace.IsEtale b ∧ ∃ y : A.left, (yoneda.preimage (b ≫ a)).left y = x}
